title: retargeted-PR defeats the base.sha 'trusted/reviewed base' assumption in publish-spec-grounding-review (write-token) + spec-grounded-review restore
body:
## Summary
`claude-code-review.yml`'s `on: pull_request` has **no `branches:` filter**, so a same-repo PR can be **retargeted onto any branch**, including an attacker-pushed one. Multiple jobs derive a "trusted"/"already-reviewed base" revision from `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`. For a retargeted PR, `base.sha` is the *attacker's* branch tip, not reviewed/merged default-branch content.

The retarget-hardened selection **already exists** — it was added to the `claude-review` restore in Unit 1b (#192 series / PR #204): trust `base.sha` only when `base.ref` byte-matches the default branch, else use the fetched default-branch tip. **This issue is that the same guard was NOT swept to the two sibling jobs that make the identical `base.sha`-is-trusted assumption.** So this is a **class-sweep**, not a point fix.

## Current state — the guard is in 1 of 3 jobs (verified against `main` HEAD `01e1ebe`)

| Job | `base.sha` use | Retarget guard (`base.ref`==`default_branch` else default-tip)? | Failure direction if defeated |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-review` (`:48`) | restore trusted config before the tag-mode action, `BASE_SHA` at **`:172`** | **YES** — hardened by Unit 1b (#204) | n/a (hardened) |
| `spec-grounded-review` (`:882`) | restore trusted config (read-only), `BASE_SHA` at **`:1072`** | **NO** — bare `base.sha`; received only #204's dir-replace *ordering* fix, never the retarget guard | read-only: a *wrong review*, not token misuse |
| `publish-spec-grounding-review` (`:1451`, **`pull-requests: write`**) | pins checkout `ref: base.sha` at **`:1569`** as its *primary* attacker-can't-reach-write control | **NO** — bare `base.sha` | **potential fail-open on a write-capable surface** |

I confirmed the `BASE_REF`/`DEFAULT_BRANCH` guard appears **only** inside `claude-review` (nowhere below line 800).

## Instances (detail)
1. **`publish-spec-grounding-review` (privileged, `pull-requests: write`) — the crux.** The checkout at `:1569` pins `ref: base.sha`, with an explicit comment that this means "every `scripts/factory/*.mts` file this job ever executes is ALWAYS the already-reviewed, already-merged base version." **That assumption holds only when the base is the protected default branch.** For a same-repo PR **retargeted onto an attacker-pushed branch**, `base.sha` is the attacker's unreviewed tip, so the job would execute attacker-authored `scripts/factory/*.mts` **with the write-capable `GITHUB_TOKEN`**. The job's own self-description — "an outside attacker can't reach write capability here at all" — **rests entirely on `base.sha` being trusted**, which is exactly what the retarget defeats. It runs on same-repo non-draft PRs (`needs: spec-grounded-review`, `if: !cancelled() && needs.spec-grounded-review.result != 'skipped'`; the review is skipped only for draft/Dependabot/fork/title-only).
2. **`spec-grounded-review` base-config restore** (`:1072`) — the read-only sibling keys its trusted revision on `base.sha` unconditionally. Same retarget defeat; read-only impact (a wrong review, not token misuse).

## Attacker model
A **same-repo contributor with push access** (needed to push the attacker base branch and retarget onto it). NOT reachable by a fork PR (fork PRs are skipped / read-only) or a public commenter.

## Calibration to settle at triage (gates `ready-to-spec`; deliberately not overstated)
- **D140 push-access equivalence:** `pull-requests: write` is largely within a push-access contributor's existing capability. The *net new* capability is arbitrary **code execution** with the job token, defeating the pin's "base is reviewed" assumption. Whether that is an accepted residual under D140 is a maintainer call.
- **OAuth token presence:** verify whether `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is in the **publish** job's env (likely not — it publishes, it does not run the model). If absent, the exfil surface is the `GITHUB_TOKEN`, not the provider credential.
- The workflow **file** itself is separately guarded (workflow-edit detection + branch protection on `main`); this finding is about the `base.sha` **content** the pin trusts, not the YAML.

## Fix direction — extract one resolver, sweep all three (do NOT hand-copy)
The correct fix is **not** to paste Unit 1b's block into two more jobs. Three hand-copied instances of security-critical trusted-revision logic is precisely the drift hazard #155 was collapsed to remove — the copies diverge and the next reviewer re-derives which one is authoritative.

- **Extract the retarget-hardened trusted-revision resolution into a single shared unit** (a composite action or a small pinned script step) that computes: `base.ref` byte-equals `default_branch` ? `base.sha` : fetched default-branch tip; fail-closed if `default_branch` is unavailable; `base.ref` compared only, never passed to `git`.
- **Apply it to all three jobs**, replacing `claude-review`'s inline copy at `:172` too, so there is exactly **one** implementation and the class cannot silently drift again.
- **Priority order: the write-token `publish-spec-grounding-review` job first**, then `spec-grounded-review`. The publish job gets **its own adversarial `factory-security-reviewer` round** given the write token — it is a distinct, higher-stakes surface than the read-only sibling and must not share a single "looks fine" pass with it.
- **Class sweep before PR leaves draft** (AGENTS.md fix-the-class rule): `grep` the whole workflow set for every `base.sha`-derived "trusted"/"reviewed base" assumption, not only the two named here, and confirm the resolver covers each.

## Routing / execution
Factory-pipeline diff (`.github/workflows/**` + likely a new composite action / `scripts/factory/**`) → **`factory-security-reviewer`** (mandatory), **conventional** execution (a factory implementing-agent patch may not touch these paths). Its own adversarial round for the write-token job as above.

## Provenance
Surfaced by the Unit 1b `story-planner` contract (#192 series, PR #204); deliberately NOT folded into #204 (a privileged-credential change warrants its own review round). Body refreshed this session with the grounded three-job class view + shared-resolver framing (line anchors verified against `main` `01e1ebe`). Related: #192, #194.
